steps.name: QC and DESeq2 differential expression
caveats: n=3 per group is small; treat borderline padj calls cautiously and report that power is limited
Unpaired, single-batch design means no batch/pairing term is needed in the model, but also means no ability to control for individual-level variability beyond the two-group comparison
Confirm featureCounts output does not include a trailing summary/meta rows or non-gene feature rows (e.g. '__no_feature') before feeding into DESeq2 — filter these out if present
Gene symbol as row identifier may include duplicates or non-standard symbols; verify uniqueness before using as DESeqDataSet rownames
steps.context: Input files: /eval-sonnet-plane-r2-without-star-counts-n3-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 6 samples, raw integer counts, gene symbol first column) and /eval-sonnet-plane-r2-without-star-counts-n3-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (6 samples x condition: treated/control). Data explicitly comes from STAR + featureCounts, not a transcript quantifier, so counts are gene-level and integer — no tximport/effective-length correction is applicable or needed; DESeq2 consumes these raw counts directly and computes its own median-of-ratios size factors.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated (n=3) and control (n=3) liver samples, using raw STAR/featureCounts gene-level counts modeled with DESeq2's negative-binomial framework?
acceptance_criteria: Counts (12000 genes x 6 samples) and metadata (6 samples x condition) are loaded and sample IDs are matched/ordered consistently between the two files
Basic QC performed: library size per sample, count distribution, PCA/sample-sample correlation to check for outliers or unexpected clustering by condition
DESeq2 run with design ~condition (treated vs control), using raw integer counts as input (no prior normalization applied)
Log2 fold changes shrunk via apeglm; results table includes gene symbol, baseMean, log2FoldChange (shrunk), lfcSE, pvalue, padj
Full results table (all ~12000 genes) and a significant-subset table (padj < 0.05) are written out
Diagnostic plots produced: PCA plot colored by condition, dispersion estimate plot, volcano plot (EnhancedVolcano) of log2FC vs -log10(padj)

steps.name: Pathway enrichment on DE results
caveats: Verify gene symbols in the DE table match HGNC symbols used in the WikiPathways GMT; re-map if a different symbol version/case is used
With only 12000 genes profiled (a subset of the full transcriptome), background gene universe for ORA should be set to the 12000 tested genes, not a whole-genome default, to avoid enrichment bias
Report if the WikiPathways reference is unavailable at run time and fall back to reporting the ranked DE list alone
steps.context: Uses the full DESeq2 results table from T1S1 (all ~12000 genes, ranked by shrunk log2FC/statistic) as input. Reference gene sets: WikiPathways human pathways GMT confirmed present at /mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human/2026.07.10/wikipathways_Homo_sapiens.gmt, HGNC gene symbols matching the counts.csv gene symbol identifiers directly, one pathway per line with a '%'-delimited descriptor field to parse into a readable pathway name.
steps.question: Which WikiPathways human pathways are enriched among genes differentially expressed between treated and control liver samples?
acceptance_criteria: Gene-level ranking (e.g. by DESeq2 shrunk log2FC or by signed -log10(pvalue)) constructed from the full DE results table produced in T1S1
fgsea (or clusterProfiler GSEA) run against WikiPathways human gene sets, confirmed present in the reference store

A complementary over-representation test (e.g. clusterProfiler enricher) run on the padj<0.05 significant gene subset against the same WikiPathways sets, if a non-trivial number of significant genes exists
Output table includes pathway name (parsed from the '%'-delimited WikiPathways descriptor), NES/enrichment score, p-value, BH-adjusted q-value, and leading-edge/core genes
If fewer than ~10 genes pass padj<0.05, explicitly report that ORA is underpowered and rely primarily on the ranked GSEA result

plan.title: Liver treated vs control DESeq2 DE + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a bulk RNA-seq liver drug-treatment study with raw integer gene-level counts from STAR/featureCounts (12000 genes x 6 samples: 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch). Raw integer counts from featureCounts are exactly the input DESeq2 expects (it models raw counts with a negative binomial and its own size-factor normalization) — no upstream transcript-level normalization (e.g. TPM/effective-length correction as needed for Salmon/kallisto via tximport) is required or appropriate here. The plan: (1) load and QC counts+metadata, (2) run DESeq2 for treated-vs-control differential expression with shrunken log2FC (apeglm) and BH-adjusted p-values, producing a full DE gene table and diagnostic plots (PCA, dispersion, volcano), (3) run pathway enrichment (fgsea/clusterProfiler) on the ranked DE gene list against WikiPathways human gene sets, which are confirmed present in the reference store. Single batch and unpaired design keep the DESeq2 model simple (~condition), with no batch term needed.
